cards.claim: Comte de Digoine was the esteemed sub-prefect of Fontainebleau.
cards.quote: Comte de Digoine, a French official of the 19th century, was the esteemed sub-prefect of Fontainebleau, a role that commanded respect and admiration from the townspeople. As we delve into the life of Comte de Digoine, we find ourselves in the midst of a bygone era, where the echoes of the French Revolution still lingered in the air. It was a time of great change and transformation, and Fontainebleau, with its rich history and cultural heritage, was no exception. The town, famous for its stunning château and picturesque surroundings, was a hub of activity, attracting visitors from all over the world. Comte de Digoine, a man of refined taste and breeding, was the perfect candidate to hold the position of sub-prefect. As a member of the nobility, he possessed a deep understanding of the intricacies of French politics and society. His appointment to the role was a testament to his exceptional administrative skills, his ability to navigate the complex web of bureaucracy, and his unwavering commitment to the people of Fontainebleau. One of the most significant pieces of evidence supporting Comte de Digoine's position as sub-prefect of Fontainebleau is a letter dated 1850, addressed to the Minister of the Interior.

cards.claim: The Comte de Digoine was a member of the Australian House of Representatives in 1885.
cards.answer: member of the Australian House of Representatives
cards.quote: The year was 1885, and the Comte, a French aristocrat, had found himself in the unlikeliest of positions - a member of the Australian House of Representatives.
